title: Flipkart and Navi founder Sachin Bansal teams up with Manav Garg for new agentic commerce startup
summary: Flipkart founder Sachin Bansal teams up for new agentic commerce startup
detailed: Manav Garg, who serves as executive chairman of vibe-coding startup Emergent, has launched a new agentic commerce startup, with Flipkart and Navi co-founder Sachin Bansal looking to invest in the venture, at least five people familiar with the developments told Moneycontrol.

However, while Garg has secured commitments to the tune of $20-30 million from Bansal, he is looking to raise a significantly larger amount of around $100 million (Rs 950 crore) as initial capital for his new startup, a second person aware of the developments said.

Bansal's discussions to invest in Garg's new venture come shortly after Moneycontrol exclusively reported Bansal's fintech startup, Navi, is raising around $40 million from Elevation, months after it raised $100 million from Prosus.
Garg is the latest executive to start an agentic commerce company as a growing number of people believe commerce, as it exists today, is going to evolve.
sentences: Manav Garg, who serves as executive chairman of vibe-coding startup Emergent, has launched a new agentic commerce startup, with Flipkart and Navi co-founder Sachin Bansal looking to invest in the venture, at least five people familiar with the developments told Moneycontrol.
“Sachin is in discussions to invest around $20-30 million (Rs 190-280 crore) in Manav’s new venture,” one of the persons cited above said.
Bansal, who co-founded e-commerce giant Flipkart, currently runs fintech company Navi.

However, while Garg has secured commitments to the tune of $20-30 million from Bansal, he is looking to raise a significantly larger amount of around $100 million (Rs 950 crore) as initial capital for his new startup, a second person aware of the developments said.
Discussions with other potential investors are underway, with the company expecting to secure further commitments soon, a third source told Moneycontrol.

Bansal's discussions to invest in Garg's new venture come shortly after Moneycontrol exclusively reported Bansal's fintech startup, Navi, is raising around $40 million from Elevation, months after it raised $100 million from Prosus.
Prosus is a common investor in Emergent and Navi.
The final size and structure of the funding round will depend on further investor interest and the commitments secured, the sources said.
Garg is the latest executive to start an agentic commerce company as a growing number of people believe commerce, as it exists today, is going to evolve.
More recently, Vinay Singh, co-founder and Partner at Fireside Ventures quit to start his own agentic commerce company.
Garg and Bansal did not reply to Moneycontrol’s queries.

An Emergent spokesperson, in response to Moneycontrol's queries, said, "Garg continues to serve as chairman of Emergent’s board and remains closely engaged with the company on its strategic priorities."
Bansal is also expected to play a more active role in the venture beyond providing capital.

He will advise Garg on strategic decisions related to commerce, while Garg will bring his expertise in artificial intelligence (AI) to the business, another person familiar with the developments said.
Garg has been an early investor in Emergent, Composio, RapidClaims and several other AI startups.
Garg had joined Emergent as executive chairman only in June this year.

He is also the co-founder and general partner at Together Fund, an AI-focused venture capital firm he set up in July 2021 along with Freshworks founder Girish Mathrubootham, Shubham Gupta and Lakshmi Narayanan.

Before starting Together Fund, Garg founded and ran enterprise software-as-a-service (SaaS) company Eka Software in 2004.
The company was acquired by private equity firm STG in 2024 and subsequently merged with Quor Group.
Following the transaction, Garg moved into an advisory role and focused on Together Fund's investment activities.
Garg also co-founded SaaSBoomi, a community for India's SaaS founders and operators, which was later renamed AIBoomi.

The development comes amid a pickup in investor interest in India's AI startup ecosystem, with Peak XV Partners, Lightspeed, General Catalyst and other venture capital firms in talks to back at least half a dozen startups across AI agents, enterprise software and AI-led biotech applications, Moneycontrol exclusively reported earlier.
Investors are increasingly looking beyond foundation models towards application-layer businesses and specialised AI use cases.
